quests.instruction: The bell has rung and your teacher is at the classroom door. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk in calmly and go to your seat 🚶
options: Walk in calmly and go to your seat 🚶
Wait outside the door until everyone is seated ⏳
Find a friend and finish your chat first 💬
quests.hint: Think about what helps the class start on time.
quests.explanation: Going straight to your seat lets the lesson begin on time and keeps the doorway clear.
quests.funFact: Many teachers greet each student at the door to start the day with a friendly hello.

quests.instruction: Your teacher is taking attendance and calls your name. What do you say?
quests.correctAnswer: Say 'present' or 'here' 🙋
options: Say your friend's name 🗣️
Wave and walk away 🚶
Say 'present' or 'here' 🙋
quests.hint: Your teacher needs to know you are there.
quests.explanation: Answering when your name is called lets the teacher know you are present and safe.
quests.funFact: The word 'present' in attendance means 'here'.

quests.instruction: Which habit makes it easier to arrive at school on time?
quests.correctAnswer: Packing your bag the night before 🎒
options: Packing your bag the night before 🎒
Leaving home at the last minute ⏱️
Stopping to play on the way 🛝
quests.hint: Think about what you can prepare ahead of time.
quests.explanation: Getting ready the night before means fewer things to do in the morning rush.
quests.funFact: Many families make a checklist near the door so nothing is forgotten.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says, 'Take out your math notebook.' What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Find it and put it on your desk 📓
options: Take out your art box 🎨
Wait for a friend to get it 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
Find it and put it on your desk 📓
quests.hint: Listen carefully to which subject was named.
quests.explanation: Taking out the right notebook right away helps the lesson begin without delays.
quests.funFact: Notebooks with ruled lines, squares, or dots are made for different kinds of work.

quests.instruction: Why do you take out your materials before the lesson starts?
quests.correctAnswer: So the lesson can begin without waiting ⏱️
options: So the lesson can begin without waiting ⏱️
So your bag becomes lighter during the lesson 🎒
So you can show your friends what you have 🧸
quests.hint: Think about what happens when everyone is ready.
quests.explanation: If everyone has their things out, the teacher can begin teaching straight away.
quests.funFact: Being ready at the start can give the class extra time for learning.

quests.instruction: Your pencil breaks right before class. What is a good solution?
quests.correctAnswer: Sharpen it or take a spare pencil ✏️
options: Take a friend's pencil without asking 🫳
Wait without writing all lesson ⏳
Sharpen it or take a spare pencil ✏️
quests.hint: A quick fix keeps you working.
quests.explanation: Sharpening your pencil or using a spare lets you keep working without disturbing anyone.
quests.funFact: Many students keep one spare pencil in their pencil case.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says, 'Open your book, then read page 5.' What do you do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Open your book 📖
options: Close your book 📕
Open your book 📖
Read page 5 aloud 🗣️
quests.hint: Follow the steps in the order they were given.
quests.explanation: Instructions often have steps, and doing them in order stops confusion.
quests.funFact: The three tiny bones inside your ear are the smallest bones in your body.

quests.instruction: What does a good listener do while the teacher is explaining?
quests.correctAnswer: Look at the teacher and stay quiet 👀
options: Talk to a friend about the weekend 💬
Look at the teacher and stay quiet 👀
Draw pictures in your notebook ✏️
quests.hint: Your eyes and ears both help you listen.
quests.explanation: Looking at the speaker and staying quiet helps your brain focus on what is being said.
quests.funFact: Your brain can pick out one voice in a noisy room, which is called the cocktail party effect.

quests.instruction: You didn't hear the instruction. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Raise your hand and ask 🙋
options: Guess and hope it's right 🤷
Copy your neighbor's work 👀
Raise your hand and ask 🙋
quests.hint: It's fine to ask again.
quests.explanation: Asking politely helps you do the task properly, and other students may need to hear it again as well.
quests.funFact: Dogs can hear higher-pitched sounds than people can.

quests.instruction: Your class is going to the gym. How should you walk in the line?
quests.correctAnswer: Calmly, one behind another 🚶
options: Calmly, one behind another 🚶
In a zigzag to avoid people 🔀
Fast, so you can get there first 🏃
quests.hint: Think about the narrow hallway and other classes.
quests.explanation: Walking calmly in line keeps hallways safe and lets other classes pass by.
quests.funFact: Ants walk in lines, following scent trails left by other ants.

quests.instruction: What is the correct way to stand in line?
quests.correctAnswer: One behind the other, facing forward 🧍
options: One behind the other, facing forward 🧍
Two or three across, chatting as you go 👥
Walking backward to watch your friends 🔄
quests.hint: Everyone can see where they are going.
quests.explanation: Standing in a line, facing forward, helps everyone move together and stay safe.
quests.funFact: In Japan, people often line up in marked spots on station platforms.

quests.instruction: Your timetable says music is next. Where do you go after the bell?
quests.correctAnswer: Music Room 🎵
options: Music Room 🎵
Library 📚
Science Lab 🔬
quests.hint: Check what the timetable says.
quests.explanation: Your timetable tells you where to go next, so you don't waste time.
quests.funFact: Some schools put the room name on the timetable so students know where to go.

quests.instruction: What is break time mainly for?
quests.correctAnswer: Resting, playing, and having a snack 🧃
options: Finishing the work from the last lesson 📚
Getting ready to go home for the day 🏠
Resting, playing, and having a snack 🧃
quests.hint: Your brain and body need a rest.
quests.explanation: Break gives your mind a rest and lets you move, eat, and play before the next lesson.
quests.funFact: Short breaks can help children concentrate better when lessons start again.

quests.instruction: The bell rings to end break. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Stop playing and line up 🚶
options: Stop playing and line up 🚶
Go off to explore the school 🧭
Play one more game 🎾
quests.hint: The bell is a signal for everyone.
quests.explanation: Responding to the bell quickly helps the next lesson start on time.
quests.funFact: Many school bells today are electric and ring automatically at set times.

quests.instruction: You are thirsty during break. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Drink from your own bottle or the fountain 💧
options: Wait until you are home to have a drink ⏳
Drink from your own bottle or the fountain 💧
Take a sip from a friend's bottle if offered 🥤
quests.hint: Think about germs and about drinking enough.
quests.explanation: Drinking your own water keeps germs from spreading and gives your body the water it needs.
quests.funFact: Children's bodies need water to stay cool when they run and play.

quests.instruction: You finish lunch. What do you do with your leftover scraps and tray?
quests.correctAnswer: Put scraps in the bin and return the tray 🍽️
options: Put scraps in the bin and return the tray 🍽️
Hand your scraps to a friend to throw away 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
Leave your tray where you sat for the staff 🪑
quests.hint: Think about the next person who will sit there.
quests.explanation: Clearing your own space keeps the cafeteria clean and ready for others.
quests.funFact: Some cafeterias separate leftovers so that they can be turned into compost.

quests.instruction: A food on your plate is one you don't like. What do you say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'No, thank you,' politely 🙂
options: 'That's disgusting!' 😖
Nothing, and swap it secretly 🔄
'No, thank you,' politely 🙂
quests.hint: You can say no kindly.
quests.explanation: A polite 'no, thank you' respects the people who made the food.
quests.funFact: Tastes can change, so food you dislike now may be fine later.

quests.instruction: You have a food allergy and aren't sure what's in a dish. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask your teacher or lunch staff first ✋
options: Ask a classmate who has the same lunch 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
Check by trying a very small taste first 🍽️
Ask your teacher or lunch staff first ✋
quests.hint: Adults in the cafeteria know what is in the meal.
quests.explanation: With allergies, always check with an adult before eating, because even small amounts can be harmful.
quests.funFact: A food label lists ingredients, so you can check for allergens.

quests.instruction: The last lesson is over. What should you do before you leave the room?
quests.correctAnswer: Pack up and push in your chair 🪑
options: Walk out and pack in the hallway 🚪
Leave your books out for tomorrow 📚
Pack up and push in your chair 🪑
quests.hint: Leave your area as you would like to find it.
quests.explanation: Packing up and pushing in your chair leaves the room ready for the next day.
quests.funFact: In Japan, students often help clean their own classrooms every day.

quests.instruction: You borrowed a book from the class shelf. When should it go back?
quests.correctAnswer: Before you leave, on its shelf 📚
options: Before you leave, on its shelf 📚
When your teacher reminds you again 🔔
At the start of next week's lesson 🗓️
quests.hint: The shelf is shared with everyone.
quests.explanation: Putting it back means the next reader can find it.
quests.funFact: People have shared books through libraries for more than two thousand years.

quests.instruction: When you pack your backpack, where should the heaviest books go?
quests.correctAnswer: Close to your back 🎒
options: Right at the front, away from your back ⬅️
Close to your back 🎒
Loose on top of the lunchbox 🍱
quests.hint: It's about balance and comfort.
quests.explanation: Heavy items near your back keep the bag balanced, so it's more comfortable.
quests.funFact: Choosing a bag that fits your back size helps prevent aches.

quests.instruction: You used the class scissors for your project. What do you do when you finish?
quests.correctAnswer: Return them to their place ✂️
options: Take them to your next lesson 🎒
Return them to their place ✂️
Leave them on your desk 🗄️
quests.hint: Others need to find them where they belong.
quests.explanation: When tools go back where they came from, they are easy to find next time.
quests.funFact: In many classrooms, shared items have labels showing where they belong.

quests.instruction: A classmate lends you a pencil. What should you do afterwards?
quests.correctAnswer: Say thank you and give it back 🙏
options: Put it in your own case 👝
Say thank you and give it back 🙏
Keep it, because they have others ✏️
quests.hint: It belongs to them, not you.
quests.explanation: Returning what you borrow shows respect and builds trust.
quests.funFact: Saying 'thank you' is polite in nearly every language.

quests.instruction: After PE, where should the balls you used be put?
quests.correctAnswer: Back in the equipment box ⚽
options: Back in the equipment box ⚽
In your bag 🎒
On the classroom shelf 📚
quests.hint: They belong to the PE area.
quests.explanation: Returning PE equipment means the next class can use it and nobody trips on a stray ball.
quests.funFact: Most balls are filled with air, which is why they bounce.

quests.instruction: Your teacher gives you homework. When should you write it down?
quests.correctAnswer: Right away, in your diary 📔
options: Tonight, if you remember 🌙
Right away, in your diary 📔
Tomorrow morning 🌅
quests.hint: Write it while you still remember the details.
quests.explanation: Writing homework down right away helps you remember what to do and when it's due.
quests.funFact: A diary can show due dates, so you can plan your time.

quests.instruction: Which is the best place to do your homework?
quests.correctAnswer: A quiet, tidy table with good light 💡
options: A busy kitchen counter during dinner 🍳
A comfortable sofa with the TV on 📺
A quiet, tidy table with good light 💡
quests.hint: Concentration needs a calm space.
quests.explanation: A quiet, bright place makes it easier to focus and do your best work.
quests.funFact: Good lighting helps your eyes stay comfortable when you read or write.

quests.instruction: You've finished your homework. What should you do next?
quests.correctAnswer: Put it in your bag right away 🎒
options: Keep it at home until the teacher asks 🏠
Leave it on the table to pack later 🪑
Put it in your bag right away 🎒
quests.hint: Tomorrow morning can be busy.
quests.explanation: Packing it immediately means it can't be forgotten in the morning.
quests.funFact: Homework is called 'prep' in some schools and 'assignments' in others.

quests.instruction: It's evening. What helps you feel ready for school tomorrow?
quests.correctAnswer: Check the timetable and pack your bag 🎒
options: Wait and see what your friends bring 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
Check the timetable and pack your bag 🎒
Pack in the morning once you're awake ⏰
quests.hint: Planning ahead takes the stress out of the morning.
quests.explanation: Checking the timetable shows what you need, and packing ahead leaves time for breakfast and travel.
quests.funFact: Many students set out their uniforms the night before.

quests.instruction: Tomorrow is PE. Which item should you be sure to pack?
quests.correctAnswer: Sports shoes 👟
options: Paintbrush 🖌️
Sports shoes 👟
Dictionary 📖
quests.hint: Think about what you need for a running game.
quests.explanation: Sports shoes keep your feet safe and comfortable when running.
quests.funFact: Wearing the right shoes helps you avoid slipping or twisting an ankle.

quests.instruction: Which habit helps you feel awake and ready for lessons?
quests.correctAnswer: Going to bed at a regular time 😴
options: Skipping breakfast 🥣
Going to bed at a regular time 😴
Staying up late to finish a show 📺
quests.hint: Your brain needs rest to learn.
quests.explanation: Enough sleep helps your brain remember what you learn and focus in class.
quests.funFact: Children aged 6 to 12 usually need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep.
